title: Operator sidecar telemetry and approval fastpath (sketch)
summary: Initial sketch for a lightweight operator sidecar that lives in customer-managed networking environments to capture and sign compact audit telemetry and enable a 'fastpath' approval flow for low-risk network/operator changes.
problem_statement: Private deployments require strong auditability for network/operator changes, but full-fidelity audit streams are heavy and expensive to ship and retain. Customers want a minimal, verifiable evidence channel that supports fast approvals for low-risk ops while preserving forensic fidelity for escalations.
goals: Define a minimal sidecar agent that captures compact approval evidence with cryptographic receipts
Enable a fastpath approval API that reduces manual review latency for low-risk changes
Provide deterministic sampling and adjustable retention to limit bandwidth and storage in customer-managed networks
Make evidence verification possible without streaming full logs off-host (signed digests)
non_goals: This document does not design the full ELT pipeline or long-term cold storage for raw packet traces
Not proposing a replacement for SIEM/EDR — sidecar is complementary and intentionally compact
Does not prespecify UI for operator review — backend primitives first
success_metrics: Median approval time for low-risk change events reduced from N mins to < 30s when fastpath eligible
Reduction in telemetry egress for audit evidence by >= 60% vs full-log export for sampled workloads
>95% of verification attempts succeed with sidecar-signed receipts (no signature errors)
Number of false-positive fastpath approvals < 0.5% in first 90 days of pilot
assumptions: Customer-managed network allows a lightweight sidecar/container to run adjacent to operator tooling (K8s DaemonSet or VM sidecar)
Customers can register a public key in Redwood control plane for verifying receipts
Edge-side resource constraints (CPU/memory) are moderate; sidecar must be < 50MB resident memory typical
design_overview: Sidecar runs as a small process (container or service) on the customer host/network operator node. It instruments operator actions (API calls, configuration commits, admin SSH sessions metadata) and emits compact evidence packets: event header, minimal metadata, deterministic sample of contextual trace (bounded size), and a signed digest. Sidecar exposes two endpoints: local /approve-fastpath to request a pre-approval token for low-risk changes, and /evidence-push to emit signed evidence to configured next-hop (customer-managed collector or Redwood edge). Fastpath tokens are short-lived signed assertions that a policy engine (local or remote) deemed the change low-risk based on metadata. Evidence packets contain a canonical digest so remote verifiers can request minimal replays (snapshot-on-demand) if deeper forensics are needed.
components: Event hooks: small adapters for K8s API server audit logs, SSH session monitors, firewall/iptables commit hooks
Compact evidence schema: 1) event_id, 2) actor_id, 3) action_type, 4) resource_summary, 5) small context blob (<=8KB), 6) timestamp, 7) sidecar_signature
Local policy engine: deterministic rules + scored risk model for fastpath eligibility
Key material: support for customer-provided public key registration and HSM/KMS integration on the customer side
Uploader: batched, retryable uploader with bandwidth caps and backoff, supports alternate sinks (SFTP, customer syslog, Redwood edge)
sampling_matrix: Deterministic: sample 1 in N events per actor to preserve distribution properties
Event-type weight: high-risk events (egress gateway changes) always captured; low-risk (tag-only config) sampled
Time-based ramp: increase sampling during incidents or rollouts automatically
Adaptive: local policy can bump sampling for unusual risk signals (spikes, anomalous actor)
retention_and_privacy: Default local retention is 7 days for full context blob and 90 days for signed digests/headers. Customers can configure shorter keeping or opt for digest-only retention to minimize PII exposure. Sidecar supports field-level redaction policies before signing; redact rules applied deterministically to keep digests verifiable. All outbound evidence can be encrypted with the customer's public key prior to leaving the host.
verification_model: Remote verifier checks sidecar_signature against registered public keys; verifies canonicalization of the header and digest. For deeper verification, verifier can request the customer-managed collector to produce an on-host replay token (customer controls release). This keeps most forensic data under customer control and only sends digests by default.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (pilot): deploy sidecar to 3 internal pilot tenants in staging, run in observability-only mode (no fastpath grant), collect feedback on schema and performance. Phase 1: enable fastpath in read-only policy mode for a subset of nodal operator teams; measure approvals and false positives. Phase 2: opt-in production for early customers with SLOs and dedicated onboarding docs; integrate KMS workflow. Phase 3: GA with templates and SDKs for custom adapters.
risks_and_mitigation: Signature misuse: enforce strict key rotation and require HSM-backed keys for high-tier customers
Leakage of sensitive fields: provide strong default redaction and customer-driven scrub rules
Operational overhead: provide lightweight default config and sensible sampling presets to avoid noisy telemetry
Approval abuse: audit every fastpath grant by storing digest + policy decision to allow retroactive review
open_questions: What is final canonicalization algorithm for evidence digests (canonical JSON, CBOR, protobuf)?
Should sidecar maintain an internal sequence number per actor to aid replay ordering?
How do we integrate customer-side KMS/HSM rotation policies into Redwood verification flow?
What operator UX is required to appeal/override fastpath grants?
notes_to_self: Keep schema intentionally small; prioritize verifiability over richness. Build prototype with Go sidecar + local filesystem sink to iterate quickly. Coordinate with eng-serving-runtime and security for key APIs and with solutions-engineering for pilot customers. Ask SRE for performance target: <5ms per event signing on typical CPU. Link prototype repo in linked_artifacts once created.
next_steps: Sketch reference sidecar API and minimal PoC implementation plan
Align with security on signature verification flow and key registration API
Write integration test plan for adaptive sampling and incident ramp behavior
Identify 2 pilot customers and draft onboarding checklist
